titre: The Witcher 3 Remastered’s Mod Library Just Got a Massive Update
chapo: The Witcher 3 Remastered patch introduces 40 new cross-platform mods for players to play with
extrait: 40 cross-platform mods have been added to CD Projekt Red’s RPG One of the best features in The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered is the ability to use mods across all available platforms. CD Projekt Red included a fair number of popular mods when the Remastered version launched at the end of September, but console players had far fewer options than PC players. CD Projekt Red is looking to bridge that gap with a new update. CD Projekt Red released patch 5.02 on Nov. 26 across Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X. The update includes a plethora of tweaks and bug fixes, such as fixing some recurring problems with Photo Mode, the main attraction is the expansion of the mod library. More than 40 new cross-platform mods are now live, and more are on the way in the future. Some of the highlights include "Glowing Witcher Eyes," a more lore-accurate depiction of Geralt that leans into the creepy nature of the Witchers. You can freshen up Geralt with a new hairstyle or try out a boat race. The most impressive addition is the expansion-sized "Tales of the Witcher: Cintra," which adds a dozen quests. That should hold players over until Songs of the Past is released next year. Witcher fans will be eating well in the next few years, as CD Projekt Red has several projects ​​​​​​​indevelopment​​​​​​​. The Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past will be released next year. The DLC​​​​​​​ is about the size of the 2016 expansion Blood and Wine and will serve as a finale to Geralt's adventures. A new trilogy of games starring Ciri will kick off in 2028 with The Witcher 4. The Witcher multiplayer game Project Sirius got an encouraging update in November, when Baudelaire Welch joined the team as a senior writer specialist. They were responsible for the fan-favorite Dark Urge storyline in Baldur's Gate 3. Development of the Witcher 1 remake is currently on the back burner​​​​​​​ as the team waits for tools and assets from The Witcher 4.

titre: The Witcher 3's new patch adds 40 cross-platform mods, fixes plenty of game-breaking bugs and "various lighting issues"
chapo: Developer CD Projekt Red has rolled out a new patch for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Remastered on all platforms, which squashes dozens of bugs and adds 40 cross-platform mods with "more on the way." Read more
extrait: Developer CD Projekt Red has rolled out a new patch for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Remastered on all platforms, which squashes dozens of bugs and adds 40 cross-platform mods with "more on the way." "Two things are certain in a witcher's life: the Path never sleeps, and the work is never done," the studio wrote in its latest exhaustive list of patch notes for the decade-old game. Patch 5.02's handiest changes come from those aforementioned bug fixes, many of which once caused the game to crash entirely or simply not work as intended. One such bug caused "time to go backwards indefinitely." Another turned Geralt bald. Opening the game with outdated mods could also result in a crash on PC. All of those, plus plenty more, have been fixed. When The Witcher 3 Remastered first dropped, many players also took issue with the game's updated and sometimes "lifeless" lighting. Previous CDPR patches already targeted the lighting changes in question, but this newest patch continues to fix "various lighting issues across multiple locations and cutscenes." The studio specifically names "overly bright or dark areas" and "inconsistent lighting transitions and flickering." The Witcher 3's free remastered upgrade also gave all console owners access to mod support, though not all pre-existing PC mods were available to download for console folks. This patch is expanding the selection somewhat with 40 new cross-platform mods, including glowy eyes for Geralt and a new monster hunt - and on social media, the studio promised "more on the way." CD Projekt Red is still hard at work on two big upcoming sequels, The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2. Speaking on the former in a recent earnings call, joint-CEO Michal Nowakowski said we can expect a similar leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 as we've just seen from GTA 5 to GTA 6.
